transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood SA), Kim Tran (Product), Maya Singh (Orion ML), Derek Lowe (Orion CTO), Priya Nair (Orion Infra), Alex Romero (Orion SRE)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, do a deep dive on quantization options and performance tradeoffs for the clinical summarization workload you sent. quick introductions?
[00:18] Maya: Hi, Maya here, ML lead on the summarization project. we've got a 2k token average prompt, sometimes spiking to 3k with history. main issue is accuracy regressions after quantizing, and latency at 95th pct.
[00:30] Derek: Derek, CTO. prioritizing safety and reproducibility; we need clear auditability for any model changes.
[00:36] Priya: Priya, infra. i care about network for VPC and whether we can run this on prem, and the peering setup.
[00:43] Laura: Laura here, SE. we'll walk through quantization approaches — GPTQ, AWQ, and INT8/FP8 tradeoffs — and show how our runtime behaves with KV cache and batching.
[00:51] Diego: quick agenda: accuracy/metrics, runtime profiles, VPC/on-prem considerations, benchmark plan.

--- Summary / Background ---
[01:12] Samir: to set context, Orion currently runs a 7B family model tuned for clinical notes, single-region private deployment would be ideal. Are you planning hosted or private pilot?
[01:25] Derek: We prefer private (VPC) or dedicated. Some data can't leave our VPC. Also want the option to move whole pilot on-prem if needed.
[01:33] Samir: totally, that's supported. we'll cover peering and permissions.

--- Quantization tradeoffs ---
[02:05] Laura: so quick primer — GPTQ gives very low FP32->INT4/INT8 accuracy loss for many models, but it can be expensive offline to generate; AWQ is a newer approach that often gives similar accuracy with faster quantization, and INT8/FP8 hardware paths can give faster throughput but sometimes worse worst-case regressions.
[02:32] Maya: what about FP8? we heard FP8 on A100s gives good throughput but models trained in FP32 still have edge cases.
[02:40] Laura: FP8 depends on kernel support — on A100s you get good perf with the right ops, but quantization-aware training or post-training calibrations still matter. Also the runtime chooses kernels; if FP8 path is available we can route to those kernels, else fallback to INT8 or BF16.
[02:58] Diego: important note: GPTQ is a per-model artifact; if you have multiple fine-tuned forks you need GPTQ for each. AWQ sometimes generalizes across similar checkpoints but still needs validation.

--- Accuracy regressions / evaluation ---
[03:24] Maya: our main problem: after GPTQ on the tuned clinical model we saw ~3% drop in a custom F1 on slot-filling tasks, which is non-trivial. Is that expected?
[03:34] Laura: possible. we typically see small deltas, but clinical tasks can be sensitive—the calibration set used during quantization matters a lot. Also KV cache interactions and context window truncation can amplify issues for long prompts.
[03:50] Diego: we usually run an automated evaluation: token-level log-perplexity, plus task-specific metrics (F1, clinical-entity overlap). also do pairwise output diffs with thresholding.
[04:03] Maya: can AWQ reduce that regression compared to GPTQ?
[04:08] Laura: in some of our internal tests AWQ matched GPTQ on average, slightly better on certain layers; but it's model-dependent. We need your real prompt set and gold outputs to know.

--- Runtime: KV cache & batching ---
[04:30] Laura: runtime side — KV cache: for long-history clinical conversations, good prefix caching yields big latency wins for repeated templates. but quantization can change memory layout: some AWQ/GPTQ kernels keep KV in different formats which affects eviction and memory pressure.
[04:49] Alex: So is the cache persisted across requests in dedicated? we want warm cache across sessions.
[04:54] Diego: on Redwood Dedicated and private we support sticky routing and warming; you can pin routes to instances to keep KV warm. But note, cold-start for a 3k token context do cost a chunk.
[05:04] Priya: our infra concern: if KV is in a quantized format, does that limit fallback to other model variants? e.g., if the primary model is AWQ quantized and we fallback to FP16, do we need to reload?
[05:16] Laura: fallback requires model variant reload — we don't dynamically dequantize cached KV to a different format. fallback is a full model swap, so there is a reload cost and cache miss.

--- Batching impact ---
[05:28] Laura: batching increases throughput but increases tail latency for single-request SLOs. For clinical interactive flows you might keep batch sizes small and use priority lanes for low-latency requests. We can recommend batching policies in the pilot.
[05:40] Maya: our latency SLO is 95th < 400ms for live assist, but batch generation for background summarization can be 2-3s. Does quantization move the 95th enough to meet SLO?
[05:52] Laura: INT8/AWQ often reduces per-token latency by 20-40% on the right hardware. But if you add model reloads or cold KV, that tail can spike. We'll show profiles.

--- Benchmarking plan discussed ---
[06:15] Samir: here's what we'll do: Redwood runs AWQ and GPTQ builds, measure throughput and accuracy on your provided prompt set (2k avg). We'll run with KV warm and cold scenarios, and with different batch settings (1,4,8).
[06:29] Maya: good, and please include both token-level metrics and our F1 entity metrics.
[06:34] Laura: yes. also include memory usage, model load times, and failure/error traces.

--- VPC / on-prem notes ---
[06:50] Priya: on VPC peering: we need an IP allowlist, and for private deployment we'd like to host the runtime inside our subnet. what's needed?
[06:58] Diego: we'll need a peering setup and an S3-compatible object storage access for model artifacts, or we can send the artifacts and host locally. KMS integration for keys is supported. There is a small agent for on-prem to manage model lifecycle.
[07:12] Priya: perf over peered link — any notable latency effects for model loads?
[07:17] Laura: model loads are bandwidth heavy; for large models expect tens of seconds to a few minutes depending on network. We recommend pre-pulling or keeping a warm pool for critical routes.

--- Customer questions and back-and-forth ---
[08:00] Derek: how does Redwood handle auditability when quantized models are used in production? we need to know which model variant served each request.
[08:09] Samir: we log model id, quantization profile, runtime kernel versions, and KV cache hits per request. All that is available in Console and audit logs.
[08:18] Maya: are there any automated regression alerts?
[08:21] Laura: yes, Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals on a small holdout set and trigger alerts if task metrics change beyond thresholds. we can wire that to your slack or pager.
[08:31] Maya: great.

[09:00] Alex: during the benchmark, will you simulate traffic from our VPC and measure network hops?
[09:05] Diego: yes we'll run both in-VPC local runs (for private) and peered-hosted runs to compare; we'll attach p95/p99 network latency measurements.

--- Tradeoffs examples and anecdotes ---
[10:10] Laura: anecdote — we had a customer where GPTQ gave near-zero quality loss but the quantized kernel wasn't optimized on their hardware, so AWQ ended up being faster. conversely, another customer saw AWQ produce slightly different tokenization edge-cases on code-generation models. hence the emphasis on evaluation.
[10:34] Maya: makes sense. we cannot accept more than 1% drop on key clinical entities.
[10:38] Laura: understood — we'll tune calibration and may recommend mixed-precision: keep critical output layers at FP16, quantize middle layers. That often preserves entity extraction.

--- Deep technical dive: per-layer and outliers ---
[11:00] Laura: GPTQ does per-channel quantization which helps for outlier weights; AWQ uses a different block-wise approach that is faster but might smooth out some outliers. For very sensitive tasks we can use per-layer higher-precision overrides.
[11:18] Maya: how invasive is that to the runtime?
[11:21] Diego: runtime supports mixed-profiles; it's a model variant. switching is a model reload but otherwise supported.

--- Logs and diagnostics ---
[12:05] Laura: we'll provide a diagnostics package: token diffs, KL divergence plots, layer-wise activation histograms, and per-prompt output comparisons, plus artifacts for model binaries.
[12:17] Maya: can you compare beam or sampling randomness? some diffs are due to decoding stochasticity.
[12:22] Laura: yes we run deterministic seeds and also stochastic runs to estimate variance.

--- Pricing and pilot scope (brief) ---
[13:00] Samir: pilot pricing would be usage plus reserved capacity for the dedicated nodes during the benchmark window; we'll follow up with a quote.
[13:08] Derek: fine; need a clear scope doc.

--- Recap and next steps ---
[13:30] Samir: recap — Redwood runs AWQ and GPTQ builds, benchmark on your prompt set, include KV warm/cold, batching configs, and detailed diagnostics. We'll share spreadsheet and initial results by Aug 10.
[13:45] Maya: we'll send the prompt set and gold outputs by Aug 7. Priya will confirm VPC peering.
[13:52] Laura: I'll start the INT8/AWQ runs on our RIs-dedicated cluster and post logs.

--- Closing Q&A and micro-discussion ---
[14:10] Derek: one last question — if we decide on on-prem long-term, how much custom engineering is required?
[14:18] Diego: we have an on-prem package; typical engagement is 4-8 weeks for setup, model onboarding, and SSO/KMS integration depending on your environment.
[14:26] Derek: ok good.

[14:40] Samir: thanks everyone. we'll send meeting notes and the action items.
[14:45] Maya: thanks all.
[14:48] (call ends)
